part.text: Now I understand the full picture. The bug is in `fast_find` in `crates/regex/src/word.rs`: the fast path assumes the whole-word match is sandwiched between two `\W` codepoints and strips one codepoint from each side. But when the match begins immediately after a line terminator, the `^` alternative in `(^|\W)` matched (zero-width) instead of `\W` — so stripping eats a real character of the inner match. The `$` side is safe because `\W` is the first alternative in the suffix alternation, but the start side needs the extra bail. Let me implement the fix.

## Summary

**Root cause** (crates/regex/src/word.rs:146): `--word-regexp` is implemented via a `WordMatcher` whose regex is `(^|\W)(<pattern>)(\W|$)`. Its `fast_find` optimization assumed every match is sandwiched between two literal `\W` codepoints, so it stripped one codepoint from each end of the match to recover the inner pattern match. But when a match begins immediately after a line terminator, the zero-width `^` alternative matched instead of `\W` — so stripping removed a real character of the inner match (e.g. `some.domain.com` became `ome.domain.com`).

**Fix**: bail out of the fast path (deferring to the always-correct captures-based path) when the byte before the match is `\n`, since `^` (`StartLF`, or `StartCRLF` in CRLF mode, which always ends in `\n`) matches there. The end-of-match side needed no change: `\W` is the first alternative in the trailing `(\W|$)` alternation, so `$` can only be selected at the end of the haystack, which was already handled.

**Verification**:
- `rg -w "([\w]+[.])*domain[.](\w)+"` now matches `some.domain.com` fully on all three lines, identical to the `\b`-wrapped pattern.
- Word-semantics edge cases still hold (`foo -2 bar` matching `-2`, `x-2`/`-2x` not matching, CRLF, Unicode boundaries, multi-line iteration offsets).
